summary: Hurriyet Daily News reported that Hungary's government moved to demote central bank governor Andras Simor by merging the Magyar Nemzeti Bank with the financial regulator. Under a constitutional amendment tabled by parliament's constitutional committee on 14 December 2011, the merged body would be headed by a person appointed by President Pal Schmitt on Prime Minister Viktor Orban's nomination, and Simor would be reduced to deputy head. Parliament was due to vote on 16 December 2011. Simor said he refused to give in to what he called "bullying" by the government to leave his post before his mandate ended in March 2013. The report also says that earlier in 2011 the government changed the rules for appointing Monetary Council members, removing Simor's influence over who the external members would be. An opposition Socialist member of the committee, Gergely Barandy, said the proposal was "nothing but a re-staffing proposal hidden in a structural change idea."
source_title: Hungary seeks to demote bank chief (Hurriyet Daily News)
checked_against: Compared with the three Hungary events already recorded: the July 2010 cabinet bill cutting Simor's pay by 75% (xpatloop), the March 2024 supervisory-board law change, and the May 2025 central bank law amendments. This is a separate action at a separate date - a December 2011 constitutional amendment to merge the central bank with the regulator and demote Simor to deputy head, plus Simor's own statement about being bullied to resign.

summary: Thai PBS World reported on 10 November 2024 that the selection committee for the chair of the Bank of Thailand's board was choosing between three candidates, and that the government's nominee was Kittiratt Na-Ranong, a former finance minister and deputy prime minister under Yingluck Shinawatra. The report describes Kittiratt as a Pheu Thai Party loyalist and a staunch critic of the central bank governor, Sethaput Suthiwartnarueput. More than 800 academics and economists, four former central bank governors and former bank officials signed a statement opposing the appointment, saying: "We are deeply concerned about the implications of political intervention on monetary policy." The report notes that the board chair appoints four of the seven members of the Monetary Policy Committee and takes part in choosing the next governor, whose term was due to end in September 2025, and that the decision on the chair had already been deferred twice. The dispute followed the central bank cutting its policy rate to 2.25% while the government pressed for a further cut.
source_title: With Kittiratt card, govt threatens BOT's independence (Thai PBS World)
checked_against: Compared with the four Thailand events already recorded: the May 2001 firing of governor Chatu Mongol Sonakul, the two Prasarn Trairatvorakul disputes of 2013 (Kittiratt saying he should be replaced, and chairman Virabongsa Ramangkura pointing to the cabinet's removal power), and Paetongtarn Shinawatra's 7 May 2024 remarks on central bank independence. This is a later and different action: the November 2024 contest over the board chairmanship and the government's nomination of Kittiratt to that post.

summary: Fox News, in a report dated 11 January 2014, said President Gurbanguly Berdymukhamedov dismissed the head of Turkmenistan's central bank, Tuvakmammet Japarov, along with the chiefs of two other state-run banks. State television announced the firings. The stated reason was unspecified "flaws in their work." The report adds that the president had earlier reprimanded Japarov and other bankers for taking regular bonuses and had ordered them to repay the money. The same round of dismissals also removed the head of the state gas company Turkmengaz.
source_title: Turkmenistan president fires central bank chief, other officials (Fox News)

summary: Euromoney reported on 1 November 2005 that Ulan Sarbanov, governor of Kyrgyzstan's central bank, had been placed under house arrest in the course of a government investigation. The investigation concerned funds he transferred to the previous president, Askar Akayev, in 1999. The report does not state the specific charge and does not say wrongdoing was proven. It says Sarbanov's position had been insecure since Akayev was ousted in March 2005, and that politicians close to the new leader, Kurmanbek Bakiyev, had pressed for Sarbanov's dismissal.
source_title: Kyrgyzstan: Central banker under house arrest (Euromoney)
checked_against: Compared with the two Kyrgyzstan events already recorded, both of which are resignation letters approved by parliament with no reason given: Kubanychbek Bokontaev on 26 June 2024 and Melis Turgunbaev on 18 March 2026. This is a different person, a different date and a different kind of action - a criminal investigation and house arrest in 2005.

summary: Radio Tamazuj reported that on Monday 9 June 2025 President Salva Kiir Mayardit removed Johnny Ohisa Domian as governor of the Bank of South Sudan by presidential decree, broadcast on state-run media. The bank's first deputy governor, Addis Ababa Othow, was named to replace him. The report says no reason was given for the dismissal. It notes that the country was facing severe shortages of local currency cash and months of unpaid government salaries, but does not link those to the removal.

summary: African News Agency reported on 8 December 2021 that Guinea's military leader, Mamadi Doumbouya, dismissed Laounceny Kaba, who had headed the Central Bank of the Republic of Guinea for ten years, together with the two vice-governors, Baidy Aribot and Madjou Sow. A younger economist, Karamo Kaba, was appointed in his place. The report attributes the removal to the length of time Laounceny Kaba had held the post and to his closeness to the deposed president, Alpha Conde, and says he had made unsuccessful attempts to win the junta's confidence. The report presents that last point as a report rather than a confirmed fact; it gives no exact date for the dismissal.

summary: The Associated Press, carried by ABC News, reported that Libya's Tripoli-based presidential council, allied with Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah's government, issued a decree firing Sadiq al-Kabir as governor of the Central Bank of Libya. Al-Kabir had led the bank since October 2011. The council named Mohamed Abdul Salam al-Shukri, an economist and former deputy governor, to replace him. The report says the decree was issued late on a Sunday and gives no official reason for the firing. The dispute was over who has the authority to appoint the governor: the east-based House of Representatives and the Supreme Council of State, both of which are mandated to appoint central bank governors under the constitutional document, called the firing illegitimate.

summary: The Associated Press, carried by Fox News, reported that Dorin Dragutanu stepped down as governor of the National Bank of Moldova on Monday 21 September 2015, after weeks of street protests over $1.5 billion that disappeared from three Moldovan banks. Protesters had been camping in a Chisinau square since 6 September and demanded an investigation into the money, which vanished before a parliamentary election the previous November. The report says Dragutanu accused politicians of interfering in the bank's internal affairs and said they had tried to discredit the central bank.
